etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English philosophie, Old French philosophie, and their source, Latin philosophia, from Ancient Greek φιλοσοφία (philosophía), from φίλος (phílos, “loving”) + σοφία (sophía, “wisdom”). By surface analysis, philo- +‎ -sophy. Displaced native Old English ūþwitegung.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) An academic discipline that seeks truth through reasoning rather than empiricism, often attempting to provide explanations relating to general concepts such as existence and rationality.

quote.citation: 1661, John Fell, The Life of the most learned, reverend and pious Dr. H. Hammond‎[1]:
quote.text: During the whole time of his abode in the university he generally spent thirteen hours of the day in study; by which assiduity besides an exact dispatch of the whole course of philosophy, he read over in a manner all classic authors that are extant […]

definitions.definition: (countable) A view or outlook regarding fundamental principles underlying some domain.

quote.citation: 2012, Francesca Valensise, From Building Fabric to City Form: Reconstruction in Calabria at end of Eighteenth Century‎[2], Gangemi Editore spa, →ISBN, page 8:
quote.text: As a matter of fact the Enlightment culture was based on a philosophy inspired to an ethical laicism whose aim was to create a better society based on principles such as solidarity, equality of rights and duties, and full freedom.

definitions.definition: A calm and thoughtful demeanor; calmness of temper.
(printing, dated) Synonym of small pica (especially in French printing).

quote.text: Although I prefer small pica. Or as its[sic] sometimes known, philosophy.– Small pica, or philosophy, she said. It sounds like the title of a novel. With a girl heroine.

quote.citation: 1603, Michel de Montaigne, chapter 12, in John Florio, transl., The Essayes […], book II, London:  […]  Val[entine] Simmes for Edward Blount […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Plato hath (in my seeming) loved this manner of Philosophying, Dialogue wise in good earnest, that therby he might more decently place in sundry mouthes the diversity and variation of his owne conceits.
